The Independent — published 2026-09-29 (date confirmed from returned metadata; no time confirmed from inside article text). Search highlights (WebFetch refused for independent.co.uk). This reads as PA wire copy; treat as wire-sourced.
"Minister refuses to rule out scrapping state pension triple lock"
LUCY POWELL to Sky News: "We are committed to the triple lock. It's in our manifesto. The triple lock has has really delivered for pensioners, in this country, over the course of this Parliament."
SHARON GRAHAM (Unite) to BBC Radio 4 Today, asked about her "electoral suicide" comment: "Instead of going and trying to pick the pocket of pensioners, we need to move over to the other side of the equation and look at things like wealth taxes, way before we try to stop something like the triple lock. It's wrong, and to be fair to Andy, he hasn't said that." "When we met with Andy this week, it certainly wasn't mentioned. But I do think that it's important that Labour make sure that working-class people know that they're on their side, and this would be a direction of travel that would say the opposite to that."
Asked whether the lock should be reformed to fund social care: "What I understood the National Care Service to be was a universal benefit: everybody paid in and everybody gets out, and that is what actually the principle of that is. Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it to take away their security is wrong. I think it's morally wrong."
